goldens.comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

golden_verdicts.reason: No tool finding mentions a missing React key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem list items.

golden_verdicts.matched_finding: Silence drawer never renders in prom-only list view (broken user flow)
golden_verdicts.reason: F1 (and F0, F3) directly identify that SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never renders from the list view because rulerRule is undefined when only promRule is passed, matching the same code location and root problem described in G1.

findings.blocking_reason: The PR changes the ability layer to show menu actions for prom-only rules, but the render guards still require rulerRule, creating a newly-visible but non-functional UI path that regresses the user experience.
findings.body: SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never renders from list view — silence action silently broken. Root cause: The PR correctly updated the ability computation layer (`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) but did not update the render/action layer — menu item guards and drawer guards still require `rulerRule`. The OR-based ability logic is sound, but AND-based render guards override it, making Pause/Delete/Silence unreachable from the prom-only list view.
findings.title: SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never renders from list view — silence action silently broken

findings.blocking_reason: This is a behavioral regression: a working 'Silence notifications' core workflow is now silently broken in the prom-only list view, as the drawer guard fails when the required rule prop is undefined.
findings.body: The silence menu item in AlertRuleMenu is shown whenever `canSilence` is true, which under the new OR-logic can be satisfied purely via `grafanaSilenceAbility` (prom-rule abilities) without any rulerRule. Clicking the item sets `showSilenceDrawer=true`. However, the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is guarded by `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where `rule` is the optional RulerRuleDTO prop. In the refactored list view (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons), only `promRule` is passed and `rule` is undefined, so the drawer never renders. Users see a 'Silence notifications' menu item, click it, and nothing happens — a silently broken core workflow.
findings.evidence: Line 104: `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && (` — `rule` is the RulerRuleDTO prop, undefined when only promRule is passed. AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 126-132 shows the silence item gated only on `canSilence`, which can be true via `grafanaSilenceAbility` alone (line 96 OR-logic).
findings.suggestion: Either (a) render SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer from a prom-rule identifier when `promRule` is available and `rule` is undefined, or (b) gate the silence menu item in AlertRuleMenu on `rulerRule` presence as well, consistent with the delete/pause items, so the menu item does not appear in a state where the drawer cannot open. Option (a) preserves the intended prom-only UX; option (b) is a safe minimal fix.
findings.title: Silence drawer never renders in prom-only list view (broken user flow)

findings.blocking_reason: This is a regression of a working user-facing action — the silence button appears in the V2 list view but clicking it silently does nothing because the drawer render condition requires an undefined rulerRule prop.
findings.body: The V2 list view (GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47) passes only `promRule` to RuleActionsButtons, leaving `rule` (rulerRule) undefined. At line 104, the silence drawer render condition is `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. Since `rule` is undefined, `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(undefined)` returns false, so `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` NEVER renders from the list view even when `showSilenceDrawer` is true. The silence button may still be visible (gated by prom abilities via `||` fallback), but clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer=true` which has no effect — the drawer stays hidden. This is a silently broken user-facing action: the button appears functional but produces no result.
findings.evidence: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx line 47: `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />` — no `rule` prop passed. RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx line 104: `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && (` — gates on `rule` which is undefined. SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer.tsx line 12: `rulerRule: RulerGrafanaRuleDTO` — requires ruler rule type. The silence button visibility uses `canSilence || canSilencePromRule` (line 88-89), so the button CAN appear via prom abilities, but the drawer CANNOT render.
findings.suggestion: Either: (1) Make SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer accept a prom rule and extract UID from `promRule.labels.__alert_uid__` or equivalent field, then change the gating condition to check prom rule type instead of ruler rule type; or (2) If silencing genuinely requires ruler data, hide the silence button entirely when `rule` is undefined rather than showing a non-functional button. Option 1 is preferred since the PR's goal is to remove ruler dependency from the list view.
findings.title: Silence drawer unreachable from V2 list view — rulerRule gating makes silence action dead code

findings.blocking_reason: The finding describes a bug in a new V2 list view but does not concretely demonstrate that pause functionality was previously working in a view being replaced by this PR, so it reads as an incomplete new feature rather than a confirmed regression of existing behavior.
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu line 113 gates the pause menu item: `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (`. When AlertRuleMenu is invoked from the V2 list view, `rulerRule` is undefined (GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule). `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(undefined)` returns false, so the pause/resume menu item never renders. The `canPause` ability may be true via prom abilities (`||` fallback in useAbilities), but the menu item rendering is additionally gated on `rulerRule` being a valid grafana ruler rule. Users cannot pause Grafana-managed rules from the new list view, which is a core workflow regression.
findings.evidence: AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 113: `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (` — `rulerRule` is undefined from list view. Line 114: `<MenuItemPauseRule rule={rulerRule} ...>` — passes undefined rulerRule. GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx line 47: passes only `promRule`, not `rule`. RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx line 95: `rulerRule={rule}` — passes undefined to AlertRuleMenu.
findings.suggestion: Change the gating to also accept prom rules. Replace `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` with a check that also considers `promRule` — e.g., `(rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) || promRuleType.grafana(promRule))`. Then update MenuItemPauseRule to accept either rule type, or create a prom-compatible pause handler that uses the prom rule UID to pause via the appropriate API.
findings.title: Pause menu item unreachable from V2 list view — rulerRule gating hides pause for prom-only rules

findings.blocking_reason: The finding describes a bug in a 'new list view' but does not concretely demonstrate that delete was previously working and is now broken by this PR; missing functionality in new code is not a regression of existing behavior.
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu line 165 gates the delete menu item: `{canDelete && rulerRule && (`. When invoked from the V2 list view, `rulerRule` is undefined, so `canDelete && undefined` is falsy — the delete menu item never renders. Additionally, `handleDelete` at line 31 requires `RulerRuleDTO` as its first argument: `handleDelete: (rule: RulerRuleDTO, ...)`. Even if the gating were relaxed, the handler cannot accept a prom rule. Users cannot delete Grafana-managed rules from the new list view, which is a critical workflow regression.
findings.evidence: AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 165: `{canDelete && rulerRule && (` — `rulerRule` undefined from list view. Line 172: `onClick={() => handleDelete(rulerRule, groupIdentifier)}` — requires RulerRuleDTO. Line 31: `handleDelete: (rule: RulerRuleDTO, ...)` — type signature requires ruler rule. GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx line 47: passes only promRule. RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx line 95: `rulerRule={rule}` — undefined.
findings.suggestion: Change the gating from `canDelete && rulerRule` to `canDelete && (rulerRule || promRule)`. Update `handleDelete` to accept `RulerRuleDTO | GrafanaPromRuleDTO` and extract the rule UID from whichever type is provided. The delete API call should use the UID, which should be available from either rule type's grafana_alert.uid or labels.
findings.title: Delete menu item unreachable from V2 list view — rulerRule gating hides delete for prom-only rules

findings.blocking_reason: This is an incomplete implementation of a new capability (delete in prom-only view), not a regression of previously working behavior since the delete button was also gated by rulerRule before this PR.
findings.body: The delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule`. `canDelete` now uses OR-logic and can be true via `grafanaDeleteAbility` alone, but the second conjunct `rulerRule` requires the RulerRuleDTO prop. In the prom-only list view, `rulerRule` is undefined, so the delete item never renders even when the user is permitted to delete via prom abilities. findings.evidence: Line 165: `{canDelete && rulerRule && (`. Compare line 135 (`canDuplicate && (` — no rulerRule guard) where the handler uses `identifier` constructed from either rule or promRule. findings.blocking_reason: The finding describes an architectural/design concern about prop interface direction; the V2 list view gating likely prevents the drawer from rendering with undefined, so no concrete runtime break is demonstrated.
findings.body: The PR changed SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer's prop from `ruleUid: string` to `rulerRule: RulerGrafanaRuleDTO`. This refactor moves the drawer in the opposite direction of the PR's goal (removing ruler dependency). The drawer now extracts UID via `rulerRule.grafana_alert.uid` (line 21), which requires a full ruler rule object. Since the V2 list view only has `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`, the drawer cannot be used from the list view even if the gating in RuleActionsButtons.V2 were fixed. This is a design-level coverage gap: the component interface was made MORE dependent on ruler, not less.
findings.evidence: SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer.tsx line 12: `rulerRule: RulerGrafanaRuleDTO` — requires ruler rule type. Line 21: `const { uid } = rulerRule.grafana_alert;` — extracts UID from ruler-specific field. Git diff shows the prop changed from `ruleUid: string` to `rulerRule: RulerGrafanaRuleDTO` (+28 -22). RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx line 105: `<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} ...>` — passes undefined from list view.
findings.suggestion: Revert the prop change to accept `ruleUid: string` (or accept both `ruleUid?: string` and `rulerRule?: RulerGrafanaRuleDTO`). The drawer only needs the UID to create a silence, so accepting a string is simpler and more flexible. Callers from list view can pass `promRule.labels.__alert_uid__` or equivalent, while callers from grouped view can continue passing `rulerRule.grafana_alert.uid`.

findings.blocking_reason: This is a concrete regression: the deprecated wrapper was rewritten to delegate to a hook that hardcodes isFederated=false, causing Edit/Delete/Pause/Restore buttons to render on federated Mimir rules in legacy views where they previously did not.
findings.body:
Findings #1 (deprecation premature) and #4 (federation check removed) combine into a silent behavior regression that neither finding alone communicates. The deprecated `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` was not preserved as a behavioral safety net — it was rewritten to delegate to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (line 228: `return useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`). That new hook hardcodes `isFederated = false` (line 245, with `// TODO: Add support for federated rules`). Consequently every existing caller that still goes through the deprecated wrapper inherits the dropped federation check.

The 3 production callers identified in Finding #1 flow through this chain:
- `RuleActionsButtons.tsx` (old, non-V2) line 57: `useAlertRuleAbility(rule, AlertRuleAction.Update)` → `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule)` (line 180) → `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(...)` → `isFederated = false`.
- `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx` line 34: same chain for `AlertRuleAction.Explore`.
- `GrafanaRuleQueryViewer.tsx` line 111: same chain for `AlertRuleAction.Explore`.

For `AlertRuleAction.Update` (gated by `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable`), a non-provisioned, non-plugin federated Mimir rule now resolves to `immutableRule = false` → `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable = MaybeSupported` → `[true, isEditable]` instead of the old `[false, false]`. The Edit button renders where it previously did not.

Mitigation coverage is inconsistent across the 3 callers:
- `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx` independently checks `isFederatedRuleGroup(group)` at line 38 — mitigated.
- `RuleActionsButtons.tsx` (old) has NO `isFederatedRuleGroup` guard (grep confirms zero references) — UNMITIGATED. It is rendered for all rules including federated Mimir rules via `RuleViewer.tsx` line 126 (`<RuleActionsButtons rule={rule} rulesSource={rule.namespace.rulesSource} />`) and `RulesTable.tsx` line 329. `RuleViewer.tsx` itself uses `isFederatedRuleGroup`, confirming federated rules reach this code path.
- `GrafanaRuleQueryViewer.tsx` uses `AlertRuleAction.Explore` which maps to `[AlwaysSupported, AccessControlAction.DataSourcesExplore]` (line 266) — NOT gated by `immutableRule`, so Explore is unaffected by the regression.

The deprecation marker (Finding #1) actively obscures the regression (Finding #4): a reviewer sees `@deprecated` and reasons 'old hook, will be removed, new path is what matters.' But the refactor rewrote the old hook to delegate to the new hook, so the regression flows through to old callers. The deprecation became a conduit for the regression rather than a safety net. An individual reviewer evaluating Finding #4 in isolation would check the new V2 callers (`RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`) and miss that the old callers lost protection too. An individual reviewer evaluating Finding #1 in isolation would classify it as a documentation/migration issue and miss the live behavior regression flowing through the wrapper.

Net effect: users viewing a federated Mimir rule in the legacy rule viewer (`RuleViewer.tsx`) or legacy rules table (`RulesTable.tsx`) will now see Edit (and potentially Delete/Pause/Restore, since `RuleActionsButtons` may render those via `useAlertRuleAbility` for other actions — confirmed it uses at least `AlertRuleAction.Update`) buttons on rules that should be immutable. Attempting the action will either fail at the API or produce inconsistent state, since the backend still treats federated rules as immutable.
findings.evidence:
Verified chain in public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:
- Line 180: `useAlertRuleAbility` calls `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule)`.
- Line 222-229: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (marked `@deprecated` line 220-221) delegates via `return useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`.
- Line 245: `const isFederated = false;` with `// TODO: Add support for federated rules`.
- Line 250: `const immutableRule = isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided;` — with `isFederated` always false, federated rules are no longer immutable.
- Line 254: `const MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable = immutableRule ? NotSupported : MaybeSupported;` — now resolves to `MaybeSupported` for federated rules.
- Line 264: `[AlertRuleAction.Update]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable, isEditable ?? false]` — now `[true, isEditable]` for federated rules.

Caller verification (grep in public/app/features/alerting/unified):
- `RuleActionsButtons.tsx` line 57: `useAlertRuleAbility(rule, AlertRuleAction.Update)` — NO `isFederatedRuleGroup` guard in file (grep returned 0 matches).
- `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx` line 34: `useAlertRuleAbility(rule, AlertRuleAction.Explore)` — HAS guard at line 38 (`isFederatedRuleGroup(group)`).
- `GrafanaRuleQueryViewer.tsx` line 111: `useAlertRuleAbility(rule, AlertRuleAction.Explore)` — Explore not gated by `immutableRule` (line 266), so unaffected.

Render-site verification (grep for `<RuleActionsButtons ` excluding V2):
- `RuleViewer.tsx` line 126: `<RuleActionsButtons rule={rule} rulesSource={rule.namespace.rulesSource} />` — renders for all rules including federated (RuleViewer.tsx itself uses `isFederatedRuleGroup`).
- `RulesTable.tsx` line 329: `<RuleActionsButtons ... />`.
- `RuleListStateView.tsx` line 134: `<RuleActionsButtons compact rule={rule} ... />`.

The V2 variant (`RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`) is a separate file imported only by the new rule-list view (GrafanaRuleListItem, StateView, DataSourceGroupLoader, DataSourceRuleLoader); the legacy view paths still render the old `RuleActionsButtons.tsx`.
findings.suggestion: Restore the federation check inside `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (the deprecated wrapper) before delegating, so old callers keep their original behavior. Concretely, compute `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` and pass it into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` via an options parameter (e.g. `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule, groupIdentifier, { isFederated })`). This preserves the old contract for the 3 live callers while the new V2 path can opt in to federation handling separately. Additionally, add a regression test in `RuleActionsButtons.test.tsx` covering a federated Mimir rule asserting that the Edit button does NOT render. Until the federation check is restored, either un-deprecate `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (so reviewers don't dismiss it) or add a `@known-regression` JSDoc tag pointing to this issue so the old callers are not treated as safe-to-ignore.
findings.title: Deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities delegates old callers through the regressing useAllRulerRuleAbilities, silently re-enabling edit/delete/pause/restore on federated Mimir rules in non-V2 RuleActionsButtons

findings.blocking_reason: The finding does not demonstrate that this PR specifically introduces the missing federation guard (it appears to analyze pre-existing V2 code), and it explicitly admits 'whether the backend rejects the operation is unknown,' so production data loss is not concretely established.
findings.body:
Finding 3 frames the federation regression as affecting only "existing callers of the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities". Finding 2 frames the V2 dual-call pattern as "safe but wasteful". Combined, neither is true for federated Mimir rules in the new V2 path.

The new V2 `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` calls `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` (line 53) — the non-deprecated replacement. This delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` which hardcodes `isFederated = false` (useAbilities.ts:245, with a `// TODO: Add support for federated rules` comment). For a federated Mimir cloud rule that is neither provisioned nor plugin-provided, `immutableRule` resolves to `false`, so `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable = MaybeSupported` and `Update` returns `[true, isEditable]`.

The V2 component ORs this with `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(skipToken, ...)` (lines 56-59), which returns `[false, false]` for a cloud prom rule. The OR at line 61 — `(editRuleSupported && editRuleAllowed) || (grafanaEditRuleSupported && grafanaEditRuleAllowed)` — therefore picks up the unguarded ruler branch: `canEditRule = true` when the rule is editable. The Edit button renders.

Neither `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` nor `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` (rendered at line 92 of V2, which uses `useRulerRuleAbilities` for 5 actions) has any independent `isFederatedRuleGroup` guard (confirmed by grep — zero matches). By contrast, `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx:38` and `RuleViewer.tsx:101` DO guard with `isFederatedRuleGroup(group)`, confirming federated rules are a live Mimir feature and that the codebase knows to guard against them elsewhere.

The delete path is worse: V2 → `AlertRuleMenu` `handleDelete` → `useDeleteModal` → `DeleteModal`. `DeleteModal.tsx` has NO `isFederatedRuleGroup` guard either (confirmed by grep). So a user can click Delete on a federated rule in the V2 list view and the modal will attempt the deletion — the UI no longer prevents it. Whether the backend rejects the operation is unknown, but the client-side immutability barrier that previously existed for federated rules is gone across the entire V2 path.

Finding 2's claim that the dual-call pattern is "safe" is incorrect for federated rules: the OR logic does not neutralize the unguarded branch, it amplifies it. Finding 3's claim that the regression is limited to "existing callers of deprecated hook" is also incomplete: the flagship V2 component — the intended migration target — has the same regression. The `@deprecated` directive (Finding 0) points maintainers toward a replacement that does not fix the regression; migrating to it propagates the regression rather than resolving it.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (useAbilities.ts:245) hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO comment — confirmed by reading the file.
Step 2: `useRulerRuleAbility` (useAbilities.ts:195-205) calls `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule, groupIdentifier)` at line 200 — it is the non-deprecated wrapper, NOT the deprecated path.
Step 3: `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:53` calls `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` — `rule` is `RulerRuleDTO | undefined` per the `RequireAtLeastOne` type (line 25-28). For a federated Mimir rule, `rule` is defined.
Step 4: `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:61`: `canEditRule = (editRuleSupported && editRuleAllowed) || (grafanaEditRuleSupported && grafanaEditRuleAllowed)`. For a cloud rule, the grafana branch is `[false, false]` (skipToken → undefined → all abilities false), so the OR picks up the ruler branch.
Step 5: Grep for `isFederated` in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` → 0 matches. Grep in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` → 0 matches. Grep in `DeleteModal.tsx` → 0 matches. No independent federation guard exists anywhere in the V2 path.
Step 6: Grep for `isFederatedRuleGroup` in `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx:38` and `RuleViewer.tsx:101` → both have the guard, confirming (a) federated rules are a live feature and (b) the codebase knows to guard against them — the V2 path is the exception, not the rule.
Step 7: `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` is rendered by V2 at line 92 (`<AlertRuleMenu ... handleDelete={() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)} />`), and uses `useRulerRuleAbilities` (line 58) with no federation guard, so the same regression applies to Delete, Pause, Restore, Duplicate, and Silence actions in the menu.
findings.suggestion: Pass the `CombinedRuleGroup` (or a precomputed `isFederated` boolean) into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` so the federation check is computed once at the call site that has group-level metadata, rather than hardcoded to `false`. Both the deprecated `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (which has `rule.group`) and the V2 callers (which have `groupIdentifier`) can supply this. If the V2 `RuleGroupIdentifierV2` type does not carry federation info, extend it or add an optional `isFederated` parameter. Additionally, add an `isFederatedRuleGroup` guard to `DeleteModal.tsx` and `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` as defense-in-depth, mirroring the existing guard in `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx:38`. Do not rely on the OR pattern in V2 to neutralize the regression — it does the opposite.
findings.title: Federation edit/delete regression extends to the new V2 rule-list components (not just the deprecated path) — the dual-call OR pattern propagates the unguarded result and DeleteModal has no federation guard

findings.blocking_reason: This is an incomplete refactor, not a regression or breakage — the grouped view still works as before since RulesTable was not functionally changed by this PR.

findings.blocking_reason: This is a regression of previously working behavior: federated rules were correctly marked immutable, but the refactor hardcodes isFederated=false, causing edit/delete/pause buttons to appear on federated Mimir rules where they previously did not.
findings.body:
The deprecated `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and included it in `immutableRule`, which prevented edit/delete/pause/restore/duplicate on federated rule groups (a Mimir-only feature). After the refactor, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a `// TODO: Add support for federated rules` comment (lines 243-245).

This silently changes behavior for **existing production callers** that still use the deprecated path via `useAlertRuleAbility` / `useAlertRuleAbilities`:
- `components/rules/RuleActionsButtons.tsx` line 57 — the old (non-V2) `RuleActionsButtons` still rendered in `RuleListStateView.tsx` and `RuleViewer.tsx`
- `components/rules/RuleDetailsButtons.tsx` line 34
- `GrafanaRuleQueryViewer.tsx` line 111

For a federated Mimir rule that is neither provisioned nor plugin-provided, the old code returned `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable = false` for Update/Delete/Pause/Restore. The new code returns `true` for those same actions, causing edit/delete/pause buttons to appear on federated rules where they previously did not. `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx` independently checks `isFederatedRuleGroup(group)` (line 38) so it mitigates the regression there, but `RuleActionsButtons.tsx` (old) and `GrafanaRuleQueryViewer.tsx` have no such guard.

The `isFederatedRuleGroup` function still exists in `utils/rules.ts` (line 373) and is actively used by `RuleViewer.tsx`, `RulesGroup.tsx`, `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx`, `GroupDetailsPage.tsx`, `Query.tsx`, and `ExistingRuleEditor.tsx` — confirming federated rules are a live feature, not dead code.
findings.dimension_name: Dual-hook abstraction duplication and deprecated hook coverage
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `useAlertRuleAbility(rule, AlertRuleAction.Update)` in `RuleActionsButtons.tsx` line 57 calls `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule)` (useAbilities.ts line 180).
Step 2: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (line 222) now delegates: `return useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)` (line 228).
Step 3: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (line 231) computes `const isFederated = false` (line 245) with a TODO comment, instead of the old `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`.
Step 4: `immutableRule = isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided` (line 250) — with `isFederated` always false, a non-provisioned, non-plugin federated rule has `immutableRule = false`.
Step 5: `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable = immutableRule ? NotSupported : MaybeSupported` (line 254) — now resolves to `MaybeSupported` (true) instead of `NotSupported` (false).
Step 6: `AlertRuleAction.Update` returns `[MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable, isEditable ?? false]` (line 264) — now `[true, true]` for an editable federated rule, showing the Edit button where it previously showed nothing.
findings.suggestion: Pass the `CombinedRuleGroup` (or a precomputed `isFederated` boolean) into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` so the federation check is preserved for callers that have group-level metadata. Alternatively, keep `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computing `isFederated` itself and pass it as a parameter to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule, groupIdentifier, { isFederated })` rather than hardcoding `false`. If the intent is to drop federation support in the new path, document the regression and update all callers of `useAlertRuleAbility` to add their own `isFederatedRuleGroup` check.
findings.title: Federation detection removed from useAllRulerRuleAbilities — behavior regression for existing callers of deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities

findings.blocking_reason: Architectural/indirection critique with no demonstrated production impact.
findings.body: Unjustified indirection layer. The hooks convert `skipToken` → `undefined` internally (`rule === skipToken ? undefined : rule`) before calling `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, which already accepts `undefined`. The Symbol adds no semantic value.

findings.blocking_reason: Missing test coverage for a new hook is a non-blocking test quality gap, not a build/test break or production correctness regression.
findings.body:
The test file `useAbilities.test.tsx` tests `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` at lines 151, 165, and 206 (via `RenderActionPermissions` component and direct `renderHook` calls). These tests now effectively test the delegation wrapper + `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` underneath, since `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` is a thin delegate (line 228).

However, the new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` hook (introduced in this PR at line 287) has **no tests at all** — neither in `useAbilities.test.tsx` nor anywhere else (confirmed by grep: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` appears only in `useAbilities.ts` definition and its two singular/plural wrapper callers). This is a significant coverage gap because:

1. The new hook contains nontrivial logic: `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` (a new internal hook), `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport`, `useCanSilenceInFolder`, and hardcoded `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`.
2. The silence ability computation differs from the ruler path: `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` (line 323) vs `canSilence` tuple from `useCanSilence` (line 267). This new silence logic is untested.
3. The `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported` (line 309) diverges from the ruler path which uses `isRulerAvailable` — this difference is untested.
4. `RulesTable.test.tsx` mocks `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (line 31) rather than testing the real hook, so it provides no integration coverage.

Keeping tests on the deprecated hook is acceptable during transition, but the **new hook must also have tests** before the old one is removed.
findings.dimension_name: Dual-hook abstraction duplication and deprecated hook coverage
findings.evidence:
Step 1: Grep for `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` across `public/app/features/alerting/unified` returns only 3 matches, all in `useAbilities.ts` (lines 287, 387, 401) — zero matches in any test file.
Step 2: `useAbilities.test.tsx` imports `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (line 21) but does not import `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` or `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.
Step 3: `RulesTable.test.tsx` mocks `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (line 31: `jest.mocked(useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities)`) and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` (line 29), so the real hook logic is never exercised in that test file.
Step 4: The new hook's silence logic `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` (line 323) is distinct from the ruler path's `canSilence` (line 267) and has no test verifying it behaves correctly for recording rules vs alerting rules.
findings.suggestion: Add test cases for `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` mirroring the existing `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` tests: (1) grafana-managed alerting rule with full permissions, (2) silence permissions with/without folder-level `AlertingSilenceCreate`, (3) provisioned prom rule (immutable), (4) loading state. Use `getGrafanaPromRule` or equivalent mock. Also add a test verifying `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` delegation produces identical results to calling `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` directly with the same inputs.
findings.title: Zero test coverage for useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities while tests remain on deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities

findings.blocking_reason: Premature deprecation without a migration path is a code quality/documentation concern; the deprecated hook still functions correctly and no production behavior is broken.
findings.body:
`useAllAlertRuleAbilities` is marked `@deprecated Use useAllRulerRuleAbilities instead` (line 220-221), but it is still indirectly called in production by 3 components via the non-deprecated wrappers `useAlertRuleAbility` and `useAlertRuleAbilities`:

1. `components/rules/RuleActionsButtons.tsx` line 57: `useAlertRuleAbility(rule, AlertRuleAction.Update)` → calls `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule)` (line 180)
2. `components/rules/RuleDetailsButtons.tsx` line 34: `useAlertRuleAbility(rule, AlertRuleAction.Explore)` → calls `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule)`
3. `GrafanaRuleQueryViewer.tsx` line 111: `useAlertRuleAbility(rule, AlertRuleAction.Explore)` → calls `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule)`

These callers pass a `CombinedRule` (which contains both `rulerRule` and `promRule`), while the recommended replacement `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` requires a separate `RulerRuleDTO` and `RuleGroupIdentifierV2`. The migration path is not trivial — callers must extract `rule.rulerRule` and compute `groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)` themselves.

Additionally, `useAlertRuleAbilities` (plural, line 187) has **zero production callers** (confirmed by grep — only appears in its own definition and test mocks). It could be deleted outright.

The deprecation without a clear migration plan creates a split state: new V2 components use the new hooks, old components use the deprecated wrapper, and there's no documented path to unify them.
findings.dimension_name: Dual-hook abstraction duplication and deprecated hook coverage
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `useAlertRuleAbility` (line 179-185) calls `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule)` at line 180 — not marked deprecated.
Step 2: Grep for `useAlertRuleAbility` in production code (excluding tests and definitions): `RuleActionsButtons.tsx` line 57, `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx` line 34, `GrafanaRuleQueryViewer.tsx` line 111 — all pass `CombinedRule`.
Step 3: `useAlertRuleAbilities` (plural, line 187-193) — grep returns zero production callers, only test mocks in `RulesTable.test.tsx` and `PanelDataAlertingTab.test.tsx`.
Step 4: The recommended replacement `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined, groupIdentifier: RuleGroupIdentifierV2)` requires callers to destructure `CombinedRule` and compute `groupIdentifierV2` — a non-trivial migration for components that currently just pass `rule`.
findings.suggestion: Either: (1) Add a migration note to the `@deprecated` JSDoc specifying that `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` wrappers are also affected and will be removed once `RuleActionsButtons.tsx`, `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx`, and `GrafanaRuleQueryViewer.tsx` are migrated. (2) Delete `useAlertRuleAbilities` (plural) since it has zero production callers. (3) Consider providing a `useCombinedRuleAbility(rule: CombinedRule, action)` wrapper that internally calls `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule))` so the migration is mechanical for existing callers.
findings.title: Deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities still has 3 production callers via wrappers — deprecation is premature without migration path

findings.blocking_reason: Architectural DRY refactor suggestion with no demonstrated correctness, security, or behavioral impact.
findings.body:
The two hooks (`useAllRulerRuleAbilities` lines 231-281, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` lines 287-337) share near-identical structure:

**Identical logic (duplicated):**
- `isProvisioned` / `isFederated` / `isPluginProvided` → `immutableRule` computation
- `MaybeSupported` / `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable` / `duplicateSupported` pattern
- The entire `abilities` object shape with all 10 `AlertRuleAction` keys
- `toAbility` calls for `Duplicate`, `View`, `Explore`
- `[MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable, isEditable ?? false]` for `Update`, `Delete`
- `[MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule, isEditable ?? false]` for `Pause`, `Restore`
- `(isRemovable && isAdmin()) ?? false` for `DeletePermanently`

**Differences (genuinely distinct):**
- Editability source: `useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, rule)` vs `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule)`
- Silence: `useCanSilence(rule)` tuple vs `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` + `useCanSilenceInFolder(folderUid)` composed
- Permissions: `getRulesPermissions(rulesSourceName)` (dynamic) vs `getRulesPermissions('grafana')` (hardcoded)
- Rule type check: `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` vs `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`
- `MaybeSupported`: `loading ? NotSupported : isRulerAvailable` vs `loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`
- `isFederated`: `false` (TODO) vs `false` (never applicable — comment explains Grafana rules can't be federated)

A `buildAbilities({ isEditable, isRemovable, isProvisioned, isFederated, isPluginProvided, isAlertingRule, rulesPermissions, canSilence: [supported, allowed], exportAllowed, maybeSupported })` function would eliminate ~50 lines of duplicated object construction while keeping the hook-specific data-gathering (calls to `useIsRuleEditable`, `useCanSilence`, etc.) in each hook. The `abilities` object construction and `immutableRule`/`MaybeSupported` derivation would live in one place, making it easier to add new actions or fix bugs in one location.
findings.dimension_name: Dual-hook abstraction duplication and deprecated hook coverage
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` lines 241-278: `useMemo` computes `isProvisioned`, `isFederated`, `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule`, `isPluginProvided`, `immutableRule`, `MaybeSupported`, `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable`, `duplicateSupported`, then builds a 10-key `abilities` object.
Step 2: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` lines 295-334: same `useMemo` structure, same `immutableRule`/`MaybeSupported`/`MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable`/`duplicateSupported` derivation, same 10-key `abilities` object with identical key structure — only the source values differ.
Step 3: Diff between the two `abilities` objects: `Silence` key differs (line 267 `canSilence` vs line 323 `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]`), `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule` variable renamed to `isAlertingRule` but used identically in both. All other keys are structurally identical with different variable sources.
findings.title: useAllRulerRuleAbilities and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities share ~80% identical logic — extract buildAbilities helper to reduce duplication
